transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-15 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~48m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Priya (CISO, Starlight Health), Tom (Eng Manager), Lina (IT Ops)

Summary: Quick security + integration review focused on SSO (SAML), SCIM for user provisioning, and RBAC model. Also touched on audit logs, KMS/encryption, SOC2/ISO artifacts, and data residency for PHI-sensitive flows. Agreed next actions: send security packet, provision a test org with SCIM, and schedule a technical POC for private deployment.

Topics: SAML metadata exchange; SCIM attribute mapping and groups; RBAC roles and least-privilege; audit logs retention and access; KMS/HSM options and envelope encryption; SOC2/ISO evidence; data residency options (US-east vs EU regions).

Transcript: 
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, im Maya from Redwood, im the AE on this account, and daniel my SE will go through the technical pieces, and then we can jump into your questions.
[00:10] Priya: thanks Maya, quick context, we’re evaluating Redwood for patient-facing summarization features, so HIPAA-ish, we need to understand SSO, SCIM provisioning and RBAC so we can map to least-privilege. also need SOC2 / ISO evidence.
[00:25] Daniel: great, thanks Priya. quick q, do you currently use Okta for SSO and SCIM? or something else?
[00:30] Tom: we use Okta for SSO and SCIM today, yes. some teams use Azure AD for service accounts but core users are in Okta.
[00:37] Lina: and we have a central idp team, they control SAML metadata and SCIM push.
[00:42] Daniel: perfect. on Redwood we support SAML2.0 SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows, and SCIM 2.0 for provisioning. we also support group sync and the common attributes (userName, givenName, familyName, emails, externalId, and custom attributes). should map pretty clean to Okta.
[00:58] Priya: couple things - we need to ensure least-privilege. can you describe the RBAC model and how roles map to API keys / tokens? we don’t want broad admin keys floating around.
[01:08] Maya: yes absolutely. our RBAC model is role-based at the org and project level. roles like Admin, Developer, Auditor, Read-only, and Operator. API tokens are scoped per-role and can be restricted to specific projects and models. we also offer short-lived session tokens and recommended rotation policies.
[01:25] Daniel: adding on, for dedicated/private deployments we can integrate with your KMS (customer-managed keys) via KMS/HSM integrations — envelope encryption so logs and payloads are encrypted with your key material.
[01:36] Tom: when you say KMS integration, do you support AWS KMS and Google KMS? any HSM options?
[01:42] Daniel: yes AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, and we have partners for HSM-backed key storage. for private on-prem installs we can support a local HSM. there’s some ops work to wire up key rotation and access controls, we can share the ops checklist.
[01:56] Priya: audit logs - how granular are they? i need to show we can produce who accessed which model, token usage, and when inference requests touched PHI. retention policy?
[02:06] Daniel: we capture per-request metadata (timestamp, user-id, project-id, model-id, route, response latencies, and anonymized token usage). audit logs can be exported to your SIEM (S3, BigQuery, or syslog) and retention is configurable. default retention is 90 days on hosted, but enterprise plans support custom retention and archiving.
[02:22] Lina: if logs contain PHI, is there an option to redact or strip PII before it lands in logs?
[02:27] Daniel: yes, we have request-level redaction options and can enable field-level scrubbing. for PHI-sensitive flows we recommend private deployment or routing through a protected pipeline with TLS + envelope encryption and redaction enabled.
[02:38] Priya: SCIM mapping — can you show an example of group to role mapping? we want groups in Okta to map to Redwood roles and projects.
[02:45] Daniel: sure. example: Okta group 'starlight-eng' -> Redwood role 'Developer' scoped to project 'patient-summaries'. SCIM groupName maps to project attribute; we can supply a mapping template. we also support attribute-level transforms for custom attributes. i will attach the mapping template after the call.
[03:03] Tom: any pitfalls we should watch for during initial sync? like duplicate externalIds or username mismatches?
[03:09] Daniel: common issues: mismatched externalId or multiple identities for same email, case sensitivity in usernames, and groups that exceed size limits. we recommend a dry-run sync against a test org and enable SCIM delta sync instead of full sync for the pilot.
[03:23] Priya: SOC2 and ISO - what artifacts can you share? we need evidence for our vendor risk assessment.
[03:28] Maya: we can share our SOC 2 Type II report redacted, ISO27001 certificate, and our security whitepaper. i’ll email the package and a link to the security portal. link: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack (note: placeholder).
[03:42] Priya: good. also need to know about data residency - we process EU patients sometimes, can you pin region?
[03:49] Daniel: yes, hosted can pin region (us-east, eu-west). for strict residency we recommend private deployment in your VPC or dedicated nodes in a region. data-in-rest and in-transit encryption applies either way.
[03:58] Lina: about RBAC least-privilege - how do you handle service accounts used by backend jobs that need model access but shouldn't have admin rights?
[04:06] Maya: create a service role with model inference permissions only, no admin. tokens can be scoped to specific models and quota-limited. we also support token minting via short-lived credentials from your identity provider in advanced setups.
[04:18] Tom: are there logs for token creation and rotation?
[04:21] Daniel: yes token lifecycle events are logged (issued, rotated, revoked) and exposed to audit log exports.
[04:26] Priya: we also need SAML metadata exchange; do you have a metadata XML we can import into Okta?
[04:32] Maya: yes, we provide SP metadata. we support both IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows and recommended binding is HTTP-POST. i will attach the metadata file and a short SAML setup doc.
[04:43] Daniel: also note SCIM provisioning requires the provisioning service to have the correct scopes in the IdP. Okta calls it 'SCIM Provisioning' with a token; we can validate the token and test in our sandbox.
[04:53] Lina: any rate limits during SCIM sync? our org has ~12k users.
[04:58] Daniel: for large orgs we do bulk provisioning endpoints and incremental delta. rate limits on hosted are adjustable for enterprise customers; for 12k users we usually recommend staggered initial import or using our bulk API.
[05:10] Priya: can we do attribute-based RBAC, like map an Okta attribute 'employeeType' -> role restrictions?
[05:15] Daniel: yes, we support attribute-based rules that map to roles; it's part of the mapping template. advanced rule engine can be discussed in the technical deep-dive.
[05:25] Tom: licensing / cost concern - if we create scoped tokens per-service account, does that multiply billing or is billing still tied to project/model usage?
[05:33] Maya: billing is usage-based (per-token/embedding units) at the project/model level; token scoping doesnt double-bill, but it can create more granular cost attribution.
[05:42] Priya: any additional controls for regulatory audits? like evidence of least-privilege enforcement or attestation logs?
[05:49] Daniel: we can provide role assignment audit trails, policy change logs, and periodic access review exports. these can be pulled into your GRC tooling.
[05:59] Priya: is there an option to restrict model variants for certain users (e.g., restrict access to models that retain less context or are quantized)?
[06:07] Daniel: yes we have model-level ACLs and per-role routing policies. you can restrict a role to a specific model family or disallow certain high-capacity models.
[06:17] Maya: recap — we will send SOC2/ISO artifacts, SAML metadata, SCIM mapping template, and RBAC template. daniel will schedule a technical deep dive to show the test org and run through an on-prem checklist.
[06:30] Priya: sounds good. please include estimated timeline for pilot and what we need from our idp team.
[06:35] Maya: will do. final note: sharing links after call: SAML guide (link), SCIM mapping template (link), RBAC least-privilege sample (link), security portal with SOC2 package (link).

End of transcript.

References/Artifacts shared: "SAML integration guide (link)", "SCIM mapping template (link)", "RBAC least-privilege sample (link)", "SOC2/ISO package (link)"
